terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the order screen loads its prices and changes its basket through named actions.

tasks.title: Keep actions beside the state
tasks.description:
Give `createStore` a second argument, `makeActions`, in `src/store.js`.

- `createStore(initial, makeActions)` calls `makeActions` once, with the store itself, the very object it returns
- what `makeActions` returns is kept as `store.actions`, so `store.actions.add(...)` calls the function it made, with its arguments, and gives back what it returns
- `store.actions` is in place by the time an action runs, so one action can call another through `store.actions`
- without `makeActions`, `store.actions` is an empty object; a `makeActions` that is not a function throws a `TypeError`

The check makes stores with actions of its own, calls them, and has one call another.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and read the error.
Keep the object `createStore` returns in a variable instead of returning it at once.
Give it an `actions` property, then fill it from `makeActions` when there is one, and return the store.
hints: An action is a function that knows how to make one change. It needs the store to do it, which is why `makeActions` is given the store.
If `makeActions` were given a copy, or ran before `store.actions` existed, an action could not reach the others. Set `store.actions` on the very object you hand it.

`const store = { getState, setState, subscribe, actions: {} }`, then `if (makeActions !== undefined) { if (typeof makeActions !== 'function') throw new TypeError('...'); store.actions = makeActions(store) }` and `return store`.

tasks.title: Name the basket's changes
tasks.description:
Implement `add`, `remove` and `reorder` in `orderActions(store)` in `src/order-actions.js`.

- `add(item, quantity)` puts `{ item, quantity }` at the end of the basket; when the basket already has a line for that item, its quantity goes up instead and it keeps its place
- `remove(item)` takes that item's line out, and the others keep their order; an item not in the basket changes nothing, so nobody is told
- `reorder(lines)` puts each line of an earlier order, an array of `{ item, quantity }`, into the basket exactly as `add` would; build it on `add`, called through `store.actions`, rather than writing the rule twice
- every change makes a new basket array and leaves the old one as it was
- the actions work when taken out of the object, as in `const { add } = store.actions`

The check runs your actions on a store of its own with a basket of its own, so they are judged even if task 1 is not done.
nextSteps: Read "An action builds on another" in the lesson.
In `add`, use `store.setState` with a function, and build the new basket from the one in the state.
In `remove`, find out first whether the item is there.
hints: The basket is an array in the state. Changing it in place gives the store the same array back, which it counts as no change: build a new one with `map`, `filter` or spread.
`some` tells you whether a line for the item is there; `map` gives a new array where one line has a new quantity; spread adds a line at the end.

In `add`: `store.setState((state) => ({ basket: found ? state.basket.map((l) => (l.item === item ? { ...l, quantity: l.quantity + quantity } : l)) : [...state.basket, { item, quantity }] }))`. In `reorder`: `for (const line of lines) store.actions.add(line.item, line.quantity)`.

tasks.title: An action that waits
tasks.description:
Implement `loadPrices()` in `src/order-actions.js`.

- at once, before it waits, it sets `loading` to `true` and `error` to `null`, so the screen can say it is loading
- it asks the price list with `fetchPrices()` from `price-list.js`, once, and waits for the answer
- when the prices come, `prices` is what the price list gave and `loading` is `false`
- when the price list fails, `loading` is `false`, `error` is the failure's message, and `prices` stays as it was
- it sets only the keys it changes, so a change made by someone else while it waits is kept
- it returns a promise that settles once the state is set, and never rejects

The check puts a price list of its own in place of yours, one that answers or fails when the check says so, and reads the state before, during and after the wait.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and look for the line that says it is loading.
Set the waiting state first, then wait for `fetchPrices()`.
Set the prices when they come, and the message when it fails.
Make sure the promise `loadPrices` returns waits for all of it.
hints: Between asking and the answer, the screen is still there and people still click. The state should say what is going on, and the rest of the state keeps changing.
An `async` function returns a promise that settles when its body has finished. `await` inside `try` lets `catch` take a failure, which keeps the promise from rejecting.

`async loadPrices() { store.setState({ loading: true, error: null }); try { const prices = await fetchPrices(); store.setState({ prices, loading: false }) } catch (error) { store.setState({ loading: false, error: error.message }) } }`.
